title: SELinux
subtitle: MAC modes, config, modules, and booleans — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Security-Enhanced Linux — extra MAC access-control layer on most modern distros (esp. RHEL/CentOS/Fedora)
cards.notes: Sits on top of DAC (chmod / owner / group).

cards.meaning: Discretionary Access Control — file owner decides with chmod / chown
cards.notes: DAC = owner’s choice.

cards.meaning: Mandatory Access Control — system policy (admin / distro) decides, not the file owner
cards.example: Even with 777, httpd may still be denied if policy says Apache must not read that path
cards.notes: Kernel still asks: does policy allow this label?

cards.meaning: Both must say yes for access to succeed
cards.notes: Memory hook: DAC = owner’s choice; SELinux = policy for the label.

cards.meaning: Policy applied and unauthorized access is blocked; violations logged
cards.notes: Enforcing = lock the door.

cards.meaning: Policy loaded but not enforced — everything allowed; violations still logged
cards.notes: Great for testing before enforcing. Door open, but write down who tried the lock.

cards.meaning: Policy not loaded; no SELinux decisions or logging
cards.notes: Disabled = no SELinux at all. Course lab often starts Disabled.

cards.meaning: Print current mode: Enforcing | Permissive | Disabled
Longer SELinux status (policy, mode, config)
cards.notes: When off: “SELinux status: disabled”.

cards.meaning: Main boot config: SELINUX= and SELINUXTYPE=
cards.notes: Reboot for mode changes to fully apply (especially enable/disable).

cards.meaning: On Red Hat, often the same file as /etc/selinux/config (symlink)
cards.notes: Edit either path.

cards.meaning: Boot default mode after reboot: enforcing | permissive | disabled
cards.notes: Change SELINUX= then reboot.

cards.meaning: Default policy type: confine selected daemons (httpd, named, …), not every process
cards.notes: targeted = jail the usual suspects (Apache, FTP…).

cards.meaning: Even smaller targeted set — only selected processes
Multi-Level Security — strict classifications; rare on ordinary servers
cards.notes: mls = military-style levels.

cards.meaning: Switch to enforcing now (only if SELinux is already enabled)
cards.notes: Temporary — does not replace editing config for boot default.

cards.meaning: Switch to permissive now — log but do not deny
cards.notes: Temporary until reboot / next setenforce.

cards.meaning: Cannot setenforce from fully disabled — needs config change + reboot
cards.notes: Often also a filesystem relabel on first enable.

cards.meaning: Set permissive, reboot, watch logs, then enforcing and reboot
cards.notes: Test in permissive before enforcing. disabled ↔ enabled always goes through a reboot.

cards.meaning: Set SELINUX=disabled in config, then reboot
List policy modules loaded in memory
cards.notes: Examples: abrt, apache, antivirus. Memory hook: which policy packs are loaded.

cards.meaning: On/off knobs inside policy (FTP home dirs, NFS, …) without writing new policy
cards.notes: Flip a named switch instead of custom policy.

cards.meaning: Catalog of policy booleans showing (current, default)
cards.notes: e.g. ftp_home_dir (off, off); mount_anyfile (on, on).

cards.meaning: Read one boolean’s current value
Turn a boolean on until reboot (not persistent)
cards.notes: Without -P lasts until reboot.

cards.meaning: Persist the boolean across reboot
cards.notes: -P = persist.
